title: The Traveller Club, Corporate Programmes and Points on a Vacation Package
content:
Holding an active traveller club membership changes what a package under Wanderlane's Vacation Package Products is charged, and the product's own terms decide everything else.

## Clauses no longer in force

Within the opening clause of this note, the wording "the club tier held on the deposit date decides the package discount applied to the price" is **no longer in force**, having been superseded by the current basis of the vacation packages charter.

So is the clause "Where the member's tier changes between deposit and departure, the discount applied at deposit stands and is neither topped up nor clawed back." Both are recorded here only so that the withdrawn wording can be recognised.

## Clauses in force

**Club and corporate are mutually exclusive.** A club discount and a corporate programme rate are mutually exclusive: a package booked under a corporate programme takes the programme's negotiated price and no club discount on top, and only a product that permits corporate booking may be booked that way at all.

**Protection bought with the package.** Travel protection bought together with the package takes the product's bundled discount, and that discount and the club insurance discount are never both applied; the larger of the two is taken.

**Points.** Club points accrue on the package price actually paid, at the earn rate of the product booked, and never on the agency service fee, port charges, gratuities or visa assistance. A package paid for entirely with a future travel credit earns no points at all.

## Points of judgement

Where a protection premium bought with the package would take a bundled discount of one size and a club insurance discount of another, one of the two is taken and it is the larger; they are not added together and they are not applied one after the other.

Where a package is booked under a corporate programme, the negotiated price of that programme is what the package is charged, and no club discount is laid on top of it. A product that does not permit corporate booking cannot be booked under a programme at all, so the question does not arise on it.
